runs.positive: A documentary photograph inside a working spacecraft assembly workshop. An exposed small upper-stage propulsion module on a low yellow steel assembly stand, centered in the foreground. Two tall curved black carbon-composite payload fairing shell halves stand upright to its left and right, open toward the camera, their interior stiffener ribs and silver bolted flanges visible. Between them a compact triangular silver tubular truss holds two black bell-shaped rocket engine nozzles. A real industrial environment with roof beams, cable trays, suspended practical lights, metal work benches, tool carts, coiled cables and distant shelving. Worn painted concrete floor with subtle oil marks and grounded contact shadows. Close inspection photograph at human eye level, 50mm lens, f5.6, natural cool window light mixed with warm practical ceiling lighting, restrained colors, detailed brushed metal, carbon fiber texture, tiny scratches, believable uneven roughness. The whole assembly is visible, two fairing halves frame the central hardware. No people, no text or labels.
